title: Network toxicology and Mendelian randomization reveal pathogenic factors of monoethyl phthalate-induced thyroid cancer.
authors: Wang, Jiao; Chen, Dandan; Zhang, Junping; Han, Xiudan; Xu, Jixiong; Liu, Ying
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过网络毒理学和孟德尔随机化分析邻苯二甲酸单乙酯致甲状腺癌的致病基因，分子对接仅涉及小分子-蛋白，未聚焦蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Monoethyl phthalate, a major metabolite of phthalate esters, is commonly found in the environment and has been linked to an increased risk of thyroid cancer. This study uses network toxicology to predict molecular initiators involved in monoethyl phthalate-induced thyroid cancer and to explore causal relationships and biological mechanisms. We identified 72 common candidate genes of monoethyl phthalate and thyroid cancer from PubChem, CTD, STITCH, GeneCards, and OMIM databases and selected 48 genes for Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. Using the IEU database and employing expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) as instrumental variables, we executed MR analysis to identify 10 monoethyl phthalate-related targets with potential causal relationship to thyroid cancer. Gene ontology and the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses highlighted that the biological processes primarily involve intracellular receptor signaling, response to estradiol, nuclear receptor activity, ligand-activated transcription factor activity, and cancer-related signaling pathways, such as the cell cycle and tryptophan metabolism. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network identified interactions between seven of these genes, revealing five core genes (ESR1, SKP2, CASP8, ARNT, and CDKN1B) as key candidate mediators in monoethyl phthalate-induced thyroid cancer. Molecular docking simulations suggested potential direct interactions between monoethyl phthalate and its protein products. Our findings propose 10 genes as potential mediators of monoethyl phthalate-induced thyroid cancer, with ESR1, SKP2, CASP8, ARNT, and CDKN1B highlighted as core factors potentially involved in thyroid cancer pathogenesis.
abstract_zh: 邻苯二甲酸单乙酯是邻苯二甲酸酯类的主要代谢产物，普遍存在于环境中，并与甲状腺癌风险增加相关。本研究利用网络毒理学预测邻苯二甲酸单乙酯诱导甲状腺癌所涉及的分子起始因子，并探讨因果关系及生物学机制。我们从PubChem、CTD、STITCH、GeneCards和OMIM数据库中鉴定了邻苯二甲酸单乙酯与甲状腺癌的72个共同候选基因，并选取48个基因进行孟德尔随机化（MR）分析。利用IEU数据库，以表达数量性状位点（eQTLs）作为工具变量，我们执行MR分析，识别出10个与甲状腺癌具有潜在因果关系的邻苯二甲酸单乙酯相关靶点。基因本体论和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）富集分析强调，生物学过程主要涉及细胞内受体信号传导、对雌二醇的反应、核受体活性、配体激活的转录因子活性以及癌症相关信号通路，如细胞周期和色氨酸代谢。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络鉴定了其中七个基因之间的相互作用，揭示出五个核心基因（ESR1、SKP2、CASP8、ARNT和CDKN1B）作为邻苯二甲酸单乙酯诱导甲状腺癌的关键候选介质。分子对接模拟提示邻苯二甲酸单乙酯与其蛋白产物之间存在潜在的直接相互作用。我们的研究结果提出10个基因作为邻苯二甲酸单乙酯诱导甲状腺癌的潜在介质，其中ESR1、SKP2、CASP8、ARNT和CDKN1B被强调为可能参与甲状腺癌发病机制的核心因子。
